atoms.b: Friction is a force that ((++slows_down speeds_up)) moving things.
The amount of friction is affected by the ((++material age)) of the object and the surface it’s travelling on.
Rough surfaces produce more friction than ((++smooth dark)) surfaces.

trainers.instruction: Decide if the scenarios are examples of friction or not.
trainers.hint: If an object is slowing down, friction is involved.

atoms.b: a rolling ball coming to a stop

atoms.a: Friction can also create other effects. Try rubbing your hands together quickly. What happens?

atoms.b: Everything needs ((++energy gravity)) to move. When friction ((++slows_down speeds_up)) a moving object, some of its moving energy is changed into ((++heat cold)) energy. This is why our hands feel warmer when we create ((++friction magnetism)) between them.

atoms.a: A shoe and a book are both at the top of a hill. Which is more likely to slide down the hill?

end.text: The sole of the shoe is much rougher than the smooth book cover. This means friction will have a greater effect on the shoe and will stop it from sliding.

atoms.text: Ravi decides to experiment with different surfaces to see which produces the least friction. He builds a ramp and measures how far the toy car travels on each surface after leaving the bottom of the ramp.

atoms.a: How should Ravi measure how far the toy car travels?

feedback.end: By using a measuring tape, Ravi’s results will be more accurate and reliable.

instruction.text: Ravi has drawn a bar chart of the results. Answer the questions about Ravi’s experiment.
instruction.sound: Ravvi has drawn a bar chart of the results. Answer the questions about Ravvi’s experiment.

atoms.a: On which surface did the toy travel furthest?
Which surface produced the least friction?
What did Ravi need to keep the same in order for his experiment to be a fair test? Select all correct answers.
b: the pen to write down each result

feedback.end: Ravi let go of the car from the same place on the ramp each time and let gravity carry it down. This made sure that the car’s initial speed was always the same and makes his results much more reliable!
